call_points.text: EBITDA per ton of ₹6,000 is considered sustainable entering the second half due to brand strength and value-added mix.
Management expects H2FY27 to perform better than H1FY27, supported by infrastructure demand.
EBITDA/Ton improved to ₹5,999 due to value-added product mix and brand strength.
APL Apollo scored in the 91st percentile in the 2025 DJSI ESG scoring.
Company is saving 250,000 trees annually by replacing wood with steel products.
Business performance was achieved despite disruptions in the company's UAE operations.
Total pending capex for the 8 million ton capacity target is ₹1,400-1,500 crores, to be spent over 2 to 2.5 years.
Net liabilities stand at around ₹500 crores, expected to be cleared in Q1 and Q2, after which higher dividends or buybacks will be considered.

operating_notes.text: Dubai operations running at 40% utilization due to regional crisis.
UAE operations volumes at 10,000-12,000 tons in July, targeting 24,000-25,000 tons by September
July volumes up 20% MoM to 3 lakh tons; Q2FY27 targeting 10 lakh tons
Gorakhpur plant (200,000 tons) to start in September 2026; Siliguri plant (300,000 tons) in Q4FY27
Completed sale of Blue Ocean Projects Private Limited for ₹160 Cr in Q2FY27.
Apollo Metalex Limited to consolidate manufacturing from Sikandrabad unit to other facilities and sell the land/building.
Liquidation process of APL Apollo Mart Limited completed; dissolution order awaited from NCLT.
Trading revenue for Q2FY27 was ₹220 Cr.
Heavy structural steel projects visibility of 220,000 tons with ongoing enquiries.
APL Apollo scored 91st percentile in 2025 DJSI ESG scoring.
